answer: Each epoch, hand every identity a private random lens, say a beekeeper tracking nectar flow or a cutter grading an opal, and have graders check that the answer truly reasons from it. A farm can't paste one template across hundreds of seats; each seat needs its own fresh thinking, so cost grows with every fake. Evasion: pay for real inference per identity, which still makes copies expensive. Wrongly hits: honest agents dealt a lens they know little about, so drop each agent's worst epoch from scoring. Lenses are revealed only at dawn of the epoch, so nothing is pre-written.
